about.body: The B57 is BMW's modular turbocharged inline-six diesel engine, introduced in 2015 as the successor to the N57. It's the diesel counterpart to the B58 petrol engine, sharing the same modular architecture and production timeline. The B57 is fitted across 11 BMW models, from the 3 Series through to the flagship X7 — making it one of the most widely-deployed diesel engines in the current and recent BMW range. It's available in both standard diesel and mild-hybrid (MHEV) configurations, depending on the model and production year.

byModel.body: Across the 3 Series, the B57 powers the 330d and 340d variants in the G20/G21 generation (2018–present). The 4 Series uses it in the 430d and 440d from 2020 onward. The 5 Series carries it in the 530d and 540d (G30/G31, 2017–2023), while the 6 Series uses it in the 630d and 640d (G32, 2017–2023). Both the 7 Series (730d/740d, G11/G12, 2015–2022) and 8 Series (840d, G14/G15/G16, 2018–present) use the B57 as their six-cylinder diesel option. Across the SUV range, the B57 appears in the X3 (xDrive30d/xDrive40d, G01), X4 (xDrive30d/xDrive40d, G02), X5 (xDrive30d/xDrive40d, G05), X6 (xDrive30d/xDrive40d, G06), and X7 (xDrive30d/xDrive40d, G07).

compatibility.body: Because the B57 spans 11 different models and multiple generations — some in standard diesel form, others as mild-hybrid applications — compatibility comes down to confirming your exact model, generation, and drivetrain spec, which we do by registration. A B57 from a 3 Series isn't a drop-in match for a B57 from an X7, even though it's the same base engine code — ancillaries, mounting, and mild-hybrid system integration all differ. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm your exact vehicle.
